findings.claim: With clear property rights and low transaction costs, parties can negotiate efficient outcomes regardless of who has the rights. Where transaction costs are high (many parties, ambiguous causation, dispersed harms), private negotiation fails and regulation or market-based interventions become necessary. (Ch 12.3)
findings.failure_mode: inherited deep-ref defect
findings.evidence: Deep 181 carries this textbook Coase-theorem wording, but the source's Coase passage (Ch 12.3, 'Better-Defined Property Rights', 16841-16859) has no transaction costs, negotiation or 'regardless of who has the rights': once a property right is clearly defined, the responsible party 'will seek out and pay for the least costly method of reducing the risk'. 'Ambiguous causation' and 'dispersed harms' are not in the source.
findings.fix: deep-fix deep 181. correct: 'Coase: until property rights are clearly defined the parties may squabble and nothing gets done; once they are, the responsible party finds the least costly fix. Pollution charges and marketable permits are the other market-oriented tools (Ch 12.3).'

notes: All [V] quotations match the converted source (externality definition 17255; nonexcludable 18457; non-rival 18465-18466; discrimination 19967; moral hazard 23092, which the source spells 'behavior' as the distillation does, while the deep's copy anglicises it; protectionism). The protectionism [V] quotes the Ch 34.1 section title, as the deep ref does; the phrase does not recur in body text. Figures check (Black/White male earnings 75.3% in 2013; immigration wage effect about 1%; cost per job saved; bilateral-monopoly employment lower and wage indeterminate). Integration rows for OB (bases of power, resource dependence, strategic contingencies, Thomas conflict modes, BATNA, cultural intelligence) and Business Ethics (Donaldson and Preston, moral minimum, triple bottom line, earth jurisprudence) match those deep refs apart from 'voiceless'. Unsupported findings cluster on three imports: Ostrom's design principles (monitoring, graduated sanctions, nested institutions), the textbook Coase theorem (which also sits unsupported in deep 181), and capture remedies (rotation, independent review). Club goods and Pareto improvement are outside the source. Key Concepts runs to 13 items against the protocol's 8-12.
